pagination.contract: Stripe v1 list data + has_more + starting_after + limit; ending_before is omitted to prevent direction mixing.

auth.selected: HTTP Basic from the encrypted Stripe connection; secret key is the username and the enrolled password slot remains connection-owned.
auth.compatibility_api_version_posture: The 36 established operations retain their existing account-version behavior as part of the byte-for-byte compatibility contract; all 574 new operations pin the audited schema version explicitly.

compatibility_secret_posture.containment: These exact legacy reads/writes retain their existing approval semantics for downstream workflow compatibility. No new workflow is published over them; every newly admitted mutation is approval-always, newly admitted reads are approval-never per D-209 §4, and secret-capable new responses are labelled.
compatibility_secret_posture.follow_up: A future runtime response-projection or secret-redaction contract can tighten these routes without silently breaking the established workflow API.

_extract.secret_response_scan: Default response graph only: x-expansionResources branches are pruned because expand is not admitted; known capability-minting routes receive a synthetic $route_capability marker.

source_decision.reason: Stripe objects are financial, customer, billing, and control-plane records rather than user-work tasks, notes, or projects. The pack therefore declares no work_entity_sources.

audit_findings_folded.finding: The previous Stripe root exposed only 36 operations and had no hash-pinned OpenAPI authority.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Preserve all 36 compatibility contracts, fill the root to 96 operations, add 12 bounded feature leaves, and pin every ingredient to the immutable official public GA spec.

audit_findings_folded.finding: A hash-pinned Stripe schema does not pin wire behavior when requests silently inherit each account's default API version.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Set static Stripe-Version 2026-06-24.dahlia on all 574 newly admitted operations. Preserve the 36 established request/approval contracts and record their inherited account-version behavior as explicit compatibility debt.

audit_findings_folded.finding: All 36 established Stripe operations parsed JSON through JavaScript numbers without the repository's unsafe-integer preservation mode.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Add response_json.unsafe_integers:string to every compatibility bind while preserving IDs, routes, arguments, risk, approval, pagination, cache behavior, and entity projections.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Stripe v1 mutations use nested form encoding while the runtime only serializes scalar form entries.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Flatten documented fields into bracket-notation keys, preserve exact integer text, require all representable documented required fields, cap optional leaves at 24, and record every omission.

audit_findings_folded.finding: POST retries can duplicate financial and control-plane mutations without stable provider idempotency keys.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Require a caller-owned Idempotency-Key on every new POST and classify each new POST as idempotent only under durable key reuse.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Stripe response schemas include client secrets, connection tokens, and other capability material, including on some reads.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Require approval on every new mutation, disable read caching, omit expand, scan the default response graph plus known capability-minting routes, label secret-capable responses, and publish no workflow over the expanded surface. Reads carry no approval gate per D-209 §4: a mark true of every read carries no sensitivity signal, and the gate belongs on the mutation.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Several of the 36 established compatibility operations can return secret or banking fields under their existing non-always read posture.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Preserve the exact compatibility API rather than silently breaking installed workflows, enumerate the inherited routes explicitly, add no new workflow over them, and require approval-always on every newly admitted mutation. Runtime response projection is recorded as the safe tightening seam.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Naive singular-keyword risk classification understates plural charge, refund, payout, transfer, top-up, reversal, and Treasury outbound-payment mutations.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Classify DELETE and monetary terminal actions as destructive, capability-minting actions as at least admin, and retain approval on every new mutation.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Per-call Stripe-Account would let a recipe redirect authority across connected accounts.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Do not expose Stripe-Account or any caller-controlled origin/auth header; connected-account tenancy remains connection enrollment authority.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Forward and reverse cursor controls cannot be combined safely in one automatic loop.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Own limit and starting_after only when the exact data/has_more/id list shape is proven; omit ending_before from those automatic operations.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Multipart upload and PDF response routes cannot be represented by the current JSON/form composition contract without semantic substitution.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Exclude the exact affected operations with media-specific reasons and retain a complete official census.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Stripe infrastructure and billing objects resemble entities but are not user-work Sources under the task/note/project rule.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Retain the existing entity projections for deterministic catalog use and declare no work_entity_sources.
